question: What serialising the RMSNorm variance reduction costs end to end. It is the only formulation measured that reproduces the single-row result, which is what the identity ladders compare against, so it is the one candidate fix that would need no re-qualification. In isolation it costs about 33x on the reduction; the reduction is a small part of a decode step, so the end-to-end figure is the one that matters.

mtp0_serialisation_inert_by_design.note: One row per step, and the knob only engages above one row, so this pair is a control on the overlay itself: -0.12%, noise.

mtp3_serialisation_active.note: Depth 3 makes the verify step 4 rows, so the reduction is split into 4 instead of 1. 172.438 against a 172.33 mean is +0.06% - no measurable cost.

single_request_cost.finding: At the strict suite's shape the 33x microbenchmark ratio does not reach the end-to-end number at all. Four sub-reductions instead of one is free against everything else a decode step does.

valid_comparison_speculative_ladder.note: Depth 3, so the verify step is 4 rows per user and the knob engages up to 16 users; 32 and 64 users exceed the 64-row threshold and are inert, which makes them controls confirming the arms are otherwise identical.
valid_comparison_speculative_ladder.finding: Free wherever it engages. The deltas scatter around zero and the +4.1% at 8 users is this ladder's known mid-rung variance, not a speedup.

invalid_first_attempt.what_happened: The no-speculation ladder was tabulated first and showed 0.0% at every rung, which was not a result: that path runs through run-server.sh, which did not forward the knob, so both arms were unserialised and the comparison was of two identical configurations. Caught by checking the container's recorded environment rather than trusting the launch.
invalid_first_attempt.fix: run-server.sh now forwards the knob conditionally, as run-w8a16-mtp1-server.sh already did.

valid_comparison_no_speculation_ladder.knob_verified_in_container: VLLM_XPU_RMSNORM_SERIAL_ROWS=64 present in the s3 ladder-mtp0 container inspect
valid_comparison_no_speculation_ladder.note: Without speculation the step is one row per user, so users == rows and 64 users is the largest engaged row count this threshold allows - the shape the 33x microbenchmark was measured at.
valid_comparison_no_speculation_ladder.finding: Free at every rung, including 64 rows where the isolated reduction costs about 33x. In the model the norm is a small fraction of a step dominated by GEMMs and the cross-card collective, and the extra launches disappear into it.

infrastructure_note: s1 aborted at its fourth server with 'server did not become healthy'. The worker died after page-size setup with no Python traceback, the signature of a cgroup OOM inside the container's 12g cap: the 9B checkpoint is 10.65 GiB, the host has 15.5 GiB, and the previous server's page cache had not been released. Three servers of the same campaign on the same code loaded fine, so this is a marginal-RAM race, not the patch. The harness now waits for MemAvailable to reach a threshold before each server rather than aborting the campaign.
identity_not_claimed: s3 was exact at every rung in both passes and its ladder gate passed, where the s0 control scored 32/31 at one rung. That is not evidence the serialisation fixed anything: the control distribution spans these outcomes and two passes cannot resolve an intervention.
verdict: The only value-preserving candidate fix - serialising the variance reduction so every batch reproduces the single-row oracle - costs nothing measurable end to end, at single-request shape and at every concurrency up to the 64-row threshold. The 33x isolated ratio is not predictive of the deployed cost. What remains unanswered is whether it actually closes the two-card identity gap: that needs the many-pass methodology from the intermittency note, not these two passes. Above 64 rows the knob does not engage and the cost is unmeasured; a production setting would need the threshold raised and re-measured.
